question.problem:
Two fair  four-sided dice are rolled and $X$ is the absolute difference of their scores. The probability mass function $f(x)$ of $X$ is shown in the table below. What is $\text{Var}[X]?$ 

| $x$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ | $3$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $\frac{2}{8}$ | $\frac{3}{8}$ | $\frac{2}{8}$ | $\frac{1}{8}$ |
question.worked_solution:
The variance of a discrete random variable $X$ with probability mass function $f(x)$ defined over a set $S$ is given by

$$
\text{Var}[X]={\sum }_{x\in S}(x-\text{E}[X])^{2}\cdot f(x).
$$

First, we need to compute $\text{E}[X].$ Summing up the products of each value of $X$ and its associated probability, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{E}[X] & =0\cdot f(0)+1\cdot f(1)+2\cdot f(2)+3\cdot f(3) \\  & =0(\frac{2}{8})+1(\frac{3}{8})+2(\frac{2}{8})+3(\frac{1}{8}) \\  & =\frac{5}{4}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $\text{E}[X]=\frac{5}{4}$ into the variance formula, we get

$$
\text{Var}[X]={\sum }_{x\in S}{(x-\frac{5}{4})}^{2}\cdot f(x).
$$

Now, we compute the variance as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Var}[X] & ={(0-\frac{5}{4})}^{2}\cdot f(0)+{(1-\frac{5}{4})}^{2}\cdot f(1)+{(2-\frac{5}{4})}^{2}\cdot f(2)+{(3-\frac{5}{4})}^{2}\cdot f(3) \\  & ={(-\frac{5}{4})}^{2}\cdot f(0)+{(-\frac{1}{4})}^{2}\cdot f(1)+{(\frac{3}{4})}^{2}\cdot f(2)+{(\frac{7}{4})}^{2}\cdot f(3) \\  & =(\frac{25}{16})(\frac{2}{8})+(\frac{1}{16})(\frac{3}{8})+(\frac{9}{16})(\frac{2}{8})+(\frac{49}{16})(\frac{1}{8}) \\  & =\frac{15}{16}\end{aligned}
$$
